title: Brutalism vs Grunge
lede: Both are described as raw. One is raw because nothing was added; the other is raw because something went wrong on purpose.
verdict: Brutalism is clean and hard: 2px black borders, a 4px offset shadow with no blur, uppercase Arial at clamp(2.6rem, 8vw, 5.4rem). Grunge is dirty: Courier New, ink that looks misregistered, rust on ash, no borders at all.
brief: Brutalism in this gallery is a system of refusals — no radius, no gradient, no soft shadow, one typeface. Depth is a 4px solid offset in pure black, which reads as a printed block rather than a floating card. Everything is uppercase and tightly tracked.

Grunge has no borders and no offsets. The "misprint" is a text-shadow pair at 2px and −1px in two different colours — a warm rust and a cold green — which imitates a second ink pass that did not line up. The depth cue is not geometry but imperfection, and the palette is ash, bone and one rust tone.

whenA: The message is a statement and the page has very little to read
You want the structure itself to be the decoration — nothing hidden, nothing softened
The brand can afford to look like a printed notice rather than a product
whenB: The subject is music, zines, or anything with an actual subculture behind it
You want texture and era without committing to a bevel or a texture image
The content is short — grunge type at 17ch gets tiring over a long read
promptDelta: The distinguishing instruction is where the imperfection lives. For brutalism, put it in the box: 2px black border and a 4px offset shadow with zero blur. For grunge, put it in the type: two offset text-shadows in different colours and no border on anything. Ask for "raw" or "brutalist grunge" and a model will combine both — heavy borders plus smeared type — which reads as a rendering fault rather than a style.
